summary: Reserved dedicated pool: gradual throughput drift leading to intermittent request timeouts after node rebalancing
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC AtlasHealth reported sustained increase in p95 latency and intermittent 504s for inference requests served from their reserved dedicated pool in us-west. Impact: customer-facing product observed degraded throughput (up to ~40% drop) and repeated request timeouts for short sequences. Timing: degradation began shortly after an automated node rebalance/scale-in event. Customer impact: degraded UX for search and chat features; support SLA threatened.

Observed symptoms: rising request queue length on pool dispatcher, elevated per-request tail latencies, GPU driver reset logs on a subset of nodes, and partial failure to recover kernels without node restart. Temporary routing to other regions not possible due to regional model pinning.

Customer contact: AtlasHealth SRE (contact: sre@atlashealth.com) opened the case and provided request ids and timestamp ranges for failed requests.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated reserved pool with mixed short conversation and batch scoring workloads pinned to redwood-7b-v1.
2) Trigger autoscaler scale-down (simulate by setting cluster usage artificially low) to cause node rebalancing/eviction.
3) Run repeated short-sequence inference requests at baseline QPS and observe queue growth and timeouts on surviving pods after node churn.
4) Check node-level nvidia-smi, driver logs, and kubelet events for signs of GPU reset or Widget state (see logs).
logs: 2026-03-10T02:13:21Z node-gpu-42 kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus: multiple reset attempts failed
2026-03-10T02:13:25Z kubelet node-gpu-42 ERROR container_runtime: failed to create container: device plugin unavailable
2026-03-10T02:14:10Z serving-runtime ERROR serve_worker[pid=12145]: KV-cache-evict thrash detected: miss_rate=0.72, growth=5x
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Patel (Support): Initial triage - customer reports p95 rising from ~120ms to ~2s and 504s starting at 02:10 UTC. Asked for recent request IDs and model pin info.

2026-03-10 03:05 Diego Alvarez (SRE): Observed 3 nodes in pool reported GPU driver resets and one node with persistent device plugin errors. Opened INT-1248 to coordinate node restarts and driver health checks.

2026-03-10 04:20 AtlasHealth SRE: Confirmed scale-in occurred at 01:58 UTC (our autoscaler) and reported a spike in short-queue requests at same time. Provided application-side traces showing increased retry latencies.

2026-03-10 06:00 Support: Performed rolling cordon/drain and restart of GPU-daemonset on 2 affected nodes; observed immediate drop in queue length but small subset of pods still degraded. Applied temporary routing to standby capacity within same region.
2026-03-11 10:15 Diego Alvarez (SRE): Deployed autoscaler hotfix (increase min_replicas for reserved pools and extend scale-in cooldown). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4627
2026-03-12 09:40 AtlasHealth: Confirmed throughput returned to baseline and timeouts ceased; requested postmortem and guidance to avoid future occurrence.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Node scale-in evicted pods while GPU driver was in a transient error state, leaving surviving pods facing a mix of warmed/unwarmed KV cache and fragmented GPU memory leading to longer setup times.
Hypothesis B: Noisy batch jobs on co-located tenants increased kernel-level contention after rebalance; autoscaler mis-sized min_replicas allowing insufficient headroom during brief traffic surges.

Findings: 1) Kernel logs show repeated NVRM GPU resets on three nodes within the reserved pool. 2) Device plugin failed startup on one node and did not re-register until kubelet restart. 3) KV-cache miss rate surged (0.72) indicating cache thrash after pod relocation. 4) Autoscaler configured with aggressive scale-in (cooldown=60s) and min_replicas set to 2 for this pool — insufficient for observed request variance during churn.

Mitigation tried in investigation: manual node restart, device-plugin restart, migrating noisy batch workload to separate pool, temporarily bumping pool min_replicas to 4. Immediate throughput improved after node restarts and min_replicas bump.

SRE action items: add detection for repeated GPU resets and an automated node-quarantine workflow, instrument KV-cache warmup tracking, revise autoscaler defaults for reserved pools to prefer more headroom during scale-in.
resolution: Resolved - Fixed and follow-up actions: Applied immediate mitigations (restarted affected GPU nodes, restarted device plugin, and increased min_replicas for AtlasHealth's reserved pool to 4). Deployed autoscaler configuration change (increase default scale-in cooldown to 300s for dedicated pools and require percent-based headroom threshold). Merged PR #4627 to platform to make these defaults configurable per-customer. Filed runbook and alert: 'gpu-reset-quarantine' to auto-cordon nodes after 2 NVRM resets within 10 minutes. Follow-ups: schedule postmortem with AtlasHealth, run regression test that simulates node churn + mixed workload. Customer confirmed baseline restored on 2026-03-12.
